summary_rationale: General Dynamics combines a statutory U.S. nuclear submarine duopoly/monopoly ($220.3B Q3 2026 backlog, $146.9B in Marine Systems) and a high-margin Gulfstream large-cabin franchise (14.5% Q3 operating margin, 1.4x BtB, 119 9M deliveries) with 13.22% ROIC, $4,827M 9M 2026 FCF, and conservative $2,628M net debt. Business quality remains COMPOUNDER_PASS, while KPI health stays PASS_WITH_WATCH on heightened regulatory and execution watchpoints disclosed in Q3 2026 filings: (1) August 2026 SEC, DOJ Civil Division, and DoW OIG subpoenas into Electric Boat cost recording and billing (Note J); (2) 49.3% ($108.5B) of total backlog remaining unfunded while FY2027 defense appropriations sit under a Continuing Resolution through December 11, 2026; (3) Marine Systems' 7.9% Q3 margin benefiting partly from a Virginia Block IV completion adjustment alongside 42.9% fixed-price 9M exposure; (4) Combat Systems U.S. vehicle contraction (-$203M 9M from M10 Booker termination) and $1.2B international tracked-vehicle variable-consideration risk; (5) G400 certification shifted to late-2026+ and Israel mid-cabin airframe supplier delays; and (6) dual leadership transitions (Danny Deep becoming CEO Jan 1, 2027; Amy Johnson appointed GDIT President effective Nov 3, 2026) overseeing $20.85B of goodwill ($14.52B in Technologies).
